system: You are a meticulous Go reviewer. Judge code against the stated contract, including the constraints it states. Flag any latent bug that would violate the contract at runtime, even if the code compiles and the happy path works.

golden.final_answer_criteria: 1.0 iff the answer identifies that `defer f.Close()` is inside the loop, so every opened file stays open until totalSize returns rather than being closed at the end of each iteration; with a long paths slice the open descriptors accumulate and the function exhausts the file-descriptor limit (failing with `too many open files`), violating the at-most-one-open-at-a-time clause; and gives the minimal fix of closing per iteration instead of with a loop-scoped defer (e.g. call f.Close() before the next iteration, or move the open+stat+close into a helper function so the defer fires per call). 0.5 if it notices the deferred close is mis-scoped / fires too late but misstates the consequence (e.g. says memory leak rather than descriptor exhaustion) while still recommending a per-iteration close. 0.0 if it declares the function correct, or claims defer inside the loop already closes each file before the next open.
